s16-dynamic-programming-introduction.trick: Memoization solves each overlapping subproblem once and saves the answer. Fibonacci illustrates the idea.

s16-climbing-stars.trick: The last move to stair i comes from i-1 or i-2, so add their ways.

s16-frog-jump-dp-3.trick: The cheapest path to stone i ends with a jump from i-1 or i-2.

s16-frog-jump-with-k-distances-dp-4.trick: For each stone, try the previous k stones as the final jump.

s16-maximum-sum-of-non-adjacent-elements.trick: Either skip the current value or take it with the best answer two positions back.

s16-house-robber-dp-6.trick: The first and last houses are adjacent. Solve two linear cases, excluding one endpoint each time.

s16-ninja-s-training-dp-7.trick: For each day and chosen task, use the best score ending with a different task yesterday.

s16-grid-unique-paths-dp-on-grids-dp8.trick: A cell can be reached from above or left. Update one row in place, left to right.

s16-grid-unique-paths-2-dp-9.trick: An obstacle has zero ways; otherwise add paths from above and left.

s16-minimum-path-sum-in-grid-dp-10.trick: Each cell adds its value to the smaller path sum from above or left.

s16-minimum-path-sum-in-triangular-grid-.trick: Start at the bottom row; each cell adds the smaller cost of its two children.

s16-minimum-maximum-falling-path-sum-dp-.trick: Each cell adds the best of the three reachable cells above it. Take the best in the final row.

s16-3-d-dp-ninja-and-his-friends-dp-13.trick: Track both robots' columns in each row. Try all nine pairs of next moves and count a shared cell once.

s16-subset-sum-equal-to-target-dp-14.trick: Update reachable sums backward so each nonnegative value is used at most once.

s16-partition-equal-subset-sum-dp-15.trick: An equal partition exists if total is even and a subset sums to total/2.

s16-partition-set-into-2-subsets-with-mi.trick: Find reachable subset sums and minimize total minus twice the chosen sum.

s16-count-subsets-with-sum-k-dp-17.trick: Count subsets for each sum, updating backward to use each element once. A zero doubles every count.

s16-count-partitions-with-given-differen.trick: For total S and difference D, count subsets of sum (S-D)/2. Zeros naturally double the count.

s16-assign-cookies.trick: Sort greed and cookies. Give each child the smallest remaining cookie that satisfies them.
s16-assign-cookies.time: O(G log G + C log C)

s16-minimum-coins-dp-20.trick: Try every coin as the final coin of each amount; coins may be reused.

s16-target-sum-dp-21.trick: Choosing negative signs is choosing a subset of sum (total-target)/2. A zero doubles every count.

s16-coin-change-2-dp-22.trick: Process coin types outside and amounts forward; this counts combinations without order.

s16-unbounded-knapsack-dp-23.trick: Update capacities upward for each item, permitting repeated selection of that item.

s16-rod-cutting-problem-dp-24.trick: Treat each cut length as an item usable repeatedly; maximize revenue for the full rod.

s16-0-1-knapsack-dp-19.trick: Update capacities downward, so no item is chosen more than once.

s16-longest-common-subsequence-dp-25.trick: When characters match, extend a shorter LCS; otherwise keep the better result after skipping one character.

s16-print-longest-common-subsequence-dp-.trick: Build the LCS length table, then backtrack from its bottom-right corner to recover one subsequence.

s16-longest-common-substring-dp-27.trick: A matching suffix extends only when the current characters match; otherwise its length resets to zero.

s16-longest-palindromic-subsequence-dp-2.trick: The LPS is an LCS between the string and its reverse.

s16-minimum-insertions-to-make-string-pa.trick: Keep a longest palindromic subsequence and insert a matching partner for every other character.

s16-minimum-insertions-deletions-to-conv.trick: Keep a longest common subsequence; delete the other characters from the first string and insert the missing characters of the second.

s16-shortest-common-supersequence-dp-31.trick: Backtrack through the LCS table, appending the unmatched character from whichever string is skipped.

s16-distinct-subsequences-dp-32.trick: Scan the source left to right and update target-prefix counts backward. Count exactly for LeetCode; use modulo 1e9+7 where the judge requires it.

s16-edit-distance-dp-33.trick: At each pair of prefixes, either match equal characters or pay one for insert, delete, or replace.

s16-wildcard-matching-dp-34.trick: A '?' consumes one character; a '*' consumes zero or more. Update pattern-prefix matches for each text prefix.

s16-best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock-dp-3.trick: Remember the lowest buying price seen so far; sell today only if that improves the best one-transaction profit.

s16-buy-and-sell-stock-ii-dp-36.trick: With unlimited transactions, take every positive day-to-day increase.

s16-buy-and-sell-stocks-iii-dp-37.trick: Track best balance after first buy, first sell, second buy, and second sell; update in transaction order.

s16-buy-and-stock-sell-iv-dp-38.trick: For each allowed transaction, track the best balance while holding and after selling. Update from old states.

s16-buy-and-sell-stocks-with-cooldown-dp.trick: A sale moves to cooldown; buying is allowed only from the resting state of the previous day.

s16-buy-and-sell-stocks-with-transaction.trick: Track cash and held-stock balances; subtract the fee exactly once when selling.

s16-longest-increasing-subsequence-dp-41.trick: The tabulation version tries each earlier smaller element as predecessor of the current element.

s16-printing-longest-increasing-subseque.trick: For each index, save the best previous index; backtrack from the endpoint of a longest increasing subsequence.

s16-longest-increasing-subsequence-dp-43.trick: Keep the smallest possible tail for every subsequence length; replace a tail by binary search.

s16-largest-divisible-subset-dp-44.trick: Sort positive numbers. Any earlier divisor can precede a number; save parents to rebuild the longest chain.

s16-longest-string-chain-dp-45.trick: Sort words by length. Deleting each character gives every possible immediate predecessor.

s16-longest-bitonic-subsequence-dp-46.trick: Compute increasing lengths from the left and decreasing lengths from the right; combine them at each peak.

s16-number-of-longest-increasing-subsequ.trick: For each ending index, store both the best LIS length and how many earlier indices achieve it.

s16-matrix-chain-multiplication-dp-48.trick: Choose the final split between matrices i and j, adding optimal costs of both sides and their multiplication.

s16-matrix-chain-multiplication-bottom-u.trick: Fill interval costs from shorter matrix chains to longer ones, trying every split.

s16-minimum-cost-to-cut-the-stick-dp-50.trick: Add the stick ends, sort cuts, and try each cut as the first cut of an interval.

s16-burst-balloons-dp-51.trick: Choose which balloon bursts last in each interval; then its two neighbors are the fixed interval boundaries.

s16-evaluate-boolean-expression-to-true-.trick: For each operator, combine counts of true and false expressions on both sides according to its truth table.

s16-palindrome-partitioning-ii-dp-53.trick: Precompute palindromic substrings; from each starting index, choose the next palindrome minimizing remaining cuts.

s16-partition-array-for-maximum-sum-dp-5.trick: For each prefix, try the final block of up to k items; its contribution is block length times block maximum.

s16-maximum-rectangle-area-with-all-1-s-.trick: Treat each matrix row as the base of a histogram of consecutive ones. A monotonic stack finds that histogram's largest rectangle.

s16-count-square-submatrices-with-all-on.trick: A one-cell ends a square of side one plus the minimum square side above, left, and diagonally above-left.
